claude.performance_metric: $870bn aggregate servicing UPB / 4.1M customers, net income $923M (FY2022); no goodwill impairment
claude.rationale: The realized record documents continuity and growth of the servicing/origination business under the surviving parent — servicing UPB rising to $870 billion across 4.1 million customers by December 31, 2022, positive net income across FY2020-FY2022, and no goodwill impairment for the Servicing, Originations and Xome reporting units. No product/operations incoherence is documented (p4=0); the sole disposition (the March 2022 Sagent technology-platform sale) was reported as a $223 million gain, not a failure. No process/organization fracture is documented — continuity of brand, headquarters and CEO (Jay Bray) with ~6,600 employees is recorded (p5=0), and nothing in the slice indicates archetype incoherence or business-model incompatibility.

grok.performance_metric: no goodwill impairment; partial MSP sale (+$223M gain); $870bn UPB retained
grok.rationale: The FY2022 10-K record shows continuity of the servicing/origination business under the same brand, HQ and CEO, with aggregate servicing UPB rising to $870bn across 4.1M customers and no goodwill impairment on Servicing/Originations/Xome units, so no product/process interface disruption is documented (p4=0). Headcount of ~6,600 and profitable operations (net income $305M/$1,454M/$923M for FY2020–22) are reported without any stated operations-vs-organization or cultural fracture, so p5=0; the sole disposition is a March 2022 technology-platform sale that recorded a $223M gain rather than a forced integration failure.

openai.performance_metric: $870 billion servicing balance across 4.1 million customers by year-end 2022
openai.rationale: No realized product/process disruption is documented; by December 31, 2022, the business serviced 4.1 million customers with an aggregate unpaid principal balance of $870 billion, and its reporting units had no goodwill impairment. No realized process/organization fracture is documented; the record instead reports approximately 6,600 employees and continued operations, while the March 2022 technology-platform sale generated a $223 million gain without being linked to integration failure.
